J U D G M E N T / AWAR D (Under Section 26 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894)
1.

This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by Virender Kumar Ors. sentences.text: the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme'
under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
LAC no. 358/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Virender Vs. Union of India Page no. 2 of 11 3.

The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.

The LAC (N/W) after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 7//19 (312), 20 (416), 8//16/2 (207), 10//24(416), 25/2 (014), 23//17 (416),
23/1(301), 24 (412), 3/2 (104) i.e. total area measuring 29 Bigha and 18 Biswas, having item nos. 412, 413 and 414 respectively, having 1/8th share each, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.
LAC no. 358/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Virender Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 11 6.
Following are the grounds under which the reference petition has been filed :

i) The LAC has not considered that the said land is very fertile and fit for all commercial, residential, industrial, etc purposes and the said land is levelled more than 2 feet height from the nearby land.
The said land bears no defects but the LAC has assessed the market value at very low rate.
ii) The revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas is situated near the National Highway No. 10, Delhi Rohtak Road and the land in question is near Main Karala Mundka Road.

The said estate is surrounded by many prestigious colonies/village/
Industries area, etc and the value of each every commodity has been raised day by Virender Kumar Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198069215/
2 day, the value of which has also been increased day by day.

sentences.text:
iii) The said Land has got potential value as many purposes and the same has been surrounded by Villages Mundka, Ghevra, Kanjhawala, Nangloi, Karala, Kirari,
Nithari, etc and it the market value is not less than Rs. 5,000/ per sq. yards.
iv) The land of the petitioners is adjacent to welldeveloped areas, colonies and hence has a great market value.

The land enjoys all type of modern facilities/ amenities like developed telephone, electricity, water connection, public school, Govt. School and most frequently severed by DTC, Railway Station and other transportation.

v) The LAC has not legally assessed the market value of the land rather he has wholly and solely relied on the policy announcement and which come into effect from the financial year 20012002 in which the LAC no. 358/ 2016 (Award No. 16/2005 06/DC(NW)) Virender Vs. Union of India Page no. 4 of 11 Government fixed the indicative prices of agricultural land at the rate of Rs.
15.70 lacs per acre for the acquisition of the Agricultural land.
The LAC has further not made any efforts to find out the market value of the land in the village.

vi) The land of the petitioners is situated on the Main road and very close to PVC market tikri,
Indian bottling Plant Ghevra, Chara Mandi Tikri, Netaje Subhash Tourism Centre, Proposed Spots Academy at Ghevra, Metro Workshop Mundka and thousands of Industries working at the time of the notification in the surrounding area.
The prestigious seats of learning Sir Chhotu Ram Polytechnic Kanjhawala, Sir Chhotu Ram High School, Haryana Shakti High School are very close to the land of petitioner.

Many developed colonies exists in the surrounding area i.e. Prem Nagar,
Rama vihar, Agar, Pratap Vihar, Bhagya Vihar.
All these factors indicate the market value of the land is not less than Rs. 5,000/ per sq. yards.

7. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming compensation for their acquired land at Rs. 5,000/ per sq.
yards.

The petitioners have claimed a solatium @ 30% on the market value and additional amount.
Interest at the amount due to the petitioners in accordance with the law and all other statutory benefits with damages of the crops @ Rs. 1,00,000/ per acre.

8. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI LAC no. 358/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Virender Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 11 and, it is, inter alia,
submitted the reference petition is not maintainable as the petitioner have failed to furnish any evidence in respect of the relief claimed in the present petition.

The Ld. LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the land in question prevailing at the time of issuance of notification under section4 of LA Act and also considering the existing locations, surroundings, availability of Civic amenities and other resources.

The possession of the land measuring 29 Bigha and 06 Biswas as also detailed in the statement U/s 19 of LA Act has been taken by the DDA and as such DDA is also a necessary party being the beneficiary of the land in question.

However, it is submitted that the Virender Kumar Ors. (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198069215/
3 Khasra No. 23/17 min possession of the land bearing 04 Bigha and 04 Biswa has not been taken and possession of the remaining portion of the land could not be taken due to built up area.

sentences.text: All the other averments made by the petitioner have been denied fully.
It is therefore submitted that the present petition is based on false, frivolous grounds and as such merits dismissal.

9. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.
LAC no. 358/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Virender Vs. Union of India Page no. 6 of 11 10.

It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.
The petitioner is also not admitted to be the owner/Bhumidhar with respect to the said land and has no locus standi to file the present petition for enhancement of compensation.
11. It is stated that the possession of the said land has been taken over by the DDA on 04.04.2006 and 07.04.2006 and after taking possession, the same was transferred to RPDVII.

All the other averments made by the petitioner in the reference petition were denied in toto and it is prayed that the prayer of the petitioner is false, frivolous and vexatious and without any cause of action,
therefore, the reference petition filed by the petitioner is level to be dismissed with cost.
LAC no. 358/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Virender Vs. Union of India Page no. 7 of 11 12.

On the basis of pleadings of the parties and documents filed on record, the following issues were framed by the court on 04.07.2015:  ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
OPP 2. Relief.
13. Matter was listed for recording of petitioners evidence.
Ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Ld.
Counsel for the respondents have submitted that they are relying upon the upon the evidence led by them in case bearing LAC no. 195 of 2016, Savitri Devi Vs. Union of India.

14. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under : 
1. Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector under Section 11 of the LA Act, if so to what amount ? OPP 15.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioners.
LAC no. 358/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Virender Vs. Union of India Page no. 8 of 11 16.
To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Savitri Devi (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
17. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

18. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Mubarakpur Dabas is covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

19. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).

The LAC no. 358/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Virender Vs.
Union of India Page no. 9 of 11 petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
20 . The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
ISSUE NO. 2/ RELIEF

As per the reference petition forwarded by LAC, the possession of land bearing Khasra No.
23//17Min (006) has not been taken which has been admitted by the petitioner.

Therefore,
petitioner is not entitled for enhancement of compensation qua this land.

22. In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioners are granted the following reliefs: (1) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,45,800/- per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/- per acre is accordingly accorded.

(2)
Additional amount @ 12% ( in terms of Section 23 (1A) of the Act). (3) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation (in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
LAC no. 358/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Virender Vs.
Union of India

Page no. 10 of 11 (4) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
23. Reference petition is accordingly, answered with parties to bear their own respective costs.
Decree sheet be drawn accordingly.
File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
ANNOUNCED IN THE OPEN COURT ON 14th DAY OF OCTOBER, 2023.
